doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Fair student, curriculum and which schools he attended
summary: He was a fair student taught reading, writing and arithmetic; they sort out the order of Douglas and Drake and a memoir error.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: As far as school was concerned, what type of student were you? Were you always . . .?

I was a fair student. I wasn’t the greatest, but I was pretty fair on all the subjects in those days. They weren’t as separate as – separated as much. There was a curriculum of standards things that were taught to you, period. That’s what you – that’s what the class is. You didn’t move from one room to the other. You had your classroom and your teacher.
Do you recall the kinds of standard things that they were teaching? Was this like . . ?
. . . McDuffy Readers kind of thing. Is it McDuffy Readers? I think it is.
Yeah. That was the reader, this McDuffy. Yeah. And there were certain named books. I can’t remember the names now, what arithmetic book became . . .
So Douglas was the first elementary.
Then Drake. How far away was that? That was on 26th and Calumet?

No, Drake was on Wentworth. It wasn’t Calumet. Calumet – it couldn’t have been Calumet, because it was on the west side of State Street. It couldn’t have been Calumet. If it’s in there that way, it’s wrong. I’m sorry. If it says Calumet, he’s wrong. Yes ma’am. That I know. “If it’s in there that way, it’s wrong” referring to page 14 of “Men, Women, and Girl Singers” that reads: “I attended the Drake School on 26th and Calumet.”
